# DebateOwl

> DebateOwl is an AI debate prep and practice app for students and competitive debaters that builds structured cases, finds the weak points in arguments, researches evidence with citations and runs timed practice rounds against an AI opponent.

DebateOwl runs at https://debateowl.com/. It is a separate product from debatelab.ai.

## Key facts (as of October 2026)

- Who it is for: students, competitive debaters and their coaches.
- 8 prep modes: Case generator, Brainstorm, Factoids, Flowchart, Case attacker, Ask coach, Crossfire and Sparring. Plus 3 utilities: Library, Debate timer and History.
- Practice: Sparring runs timed rounds against an AI opponent in School 4-6-6-3, Lincoln-Douglas and Public Forum and ends with a judged verdict. Crossfire drills cross-examination.
- Languages: English, Spanish and Hungarian.
- Pricing: As of October 2026, DebateOwl has a 3-day free trial with no credit card required, then Pro costs $5/month + tax. There is no permanent free plan.
- Pro adds expanded AI prep access, all 10 models (including Claude Opus and Sonnet, GPT-6.1 Sol and Gemini), Active Grounding research and priority support.
- Privacy: cases, sources, practice rounds and history stay behind sign-in and are not indexed.

## Free tools

Free to use, no account needed, and they run in the browser.

- [All free debate tools](https://debateowl.com/tools): every tool below on one page
- [Debate timer](https://debateowl.com/tools/debate-timer): Round timer for PF, LD, Policy, BP, World Schools and Asian Parliamentary, with protected time, POI knocks and prep banks.
- [Debate motion generator](https://debateowl.com/tools/debate-motion-generator): Draw one practice motion or three for a veto drill, from 300 original motions sorted by topic and difficulty.
- [Debate flow sheet](https://debateowl.com/tools/debate-flow-sheet): A printable one-page flow with a column for every speech in your format, on A4 or Letter.
- [Speech time calculator](https://debateowl.com/tools/speech-time-calculator): Paste a speech to see how long it takes to deliver and which speech slots it fits.

## Guides

- [AI Debate Practice for Stronger Cases, Rebuttals, and Speeches](https://debateowl.com/ai-debate-practice): Practice debate online with DebateOwl: AI opponents, targeted drills, rebuttal feedback, evidence research, argument flowcharts, and tournament-ready prep tools.
- [AI Debate Case Generator with Citations](https://debateowl.com/ai-debate-case-generator): Use an AI debate case generator to draft structured cases with claims, warrants, impacts, and evidence leads, then verify sources before round.
- [Practice Rebuttals Before Your Opponent Finds the Weakness](https://debateowl.com/debate-rebuttal-practice): Practice rebuttals with DebateOwl. Analyze arguments, find weak warrants, missing weighing, logical gaps, and cross-examination traps before your round.
- [Ask an AI Debate Coach for Round-Ready Prep](https://debateowl.com/ai-debate-coach): Ask DebateOwl's AI debate coach for help with strategy, argument structure, weighing, rebuttals, speeches, prep questions, and practice feedback.
- [Find Better Debate Evidence Without Losing the Argument](https://debateowl.com/debate-evidence-finder): Find evidence leads for debate cases with DebateOwl, then verify original sources, citations, warrants, and impact links before using them in round.
- [Map the Clash With an Argument Flowchart](https://debateowl.com/argument-flowchart): Map debate arguments, clash, links, impacts, and weighing with DebateOwl's argument flowchart workflow for clearer speeches and rebuttals.
- [How Debate Speech Times Work in Each Format](https://debateowl.com/online-debate-timer): How long debate speeches are in Public Forum, Lincoln-Douglas, Policy, British Parliamentary and World Schools, with cross-examination, prep time and drills for practising against the clock.
- [How to Write a Debate Case](https://debateowl.com/how-to-write-a-debate-case): Learn how to write a debate case with a clear motion analysis, burdens, contentions, warrants, evidence, impacts, and weighing using DebateOwl.
- [How to Practice Debate Rebuttals](https://debateowl.com/how-to-practice-rebuttals): Learn how to practice debate rebuttals with drills for warrants, evidence quality, impact weighing, cross-examination, and speech collapse.
- [Public Forum Debate Prep with AI](https://debateowl.com/public-forum-debate): Prepare for Public Forum debate with DebateOwl: case construction, rebuttal drills, summary and final focus practice, crossfire prep, and evidence research.
- [Lincoln-Douglas Debate Prep with AI](https://debateowl.com/lincoln-douglas-debate): How a Lincoln-Douglas round runs at NSDA speech times, how a value and criterion work, a worked example case and the neg turn against it, common LD mistakes and a 15-minute drill.
- [Policy Debate Prep with AI](https://debateowl.com/policy-debate): How a Policy (CX) round runs at the NSDA 8-3-5 times, what the plan, disadvantage, counterplan, topicality and kritik each have to prove, a worked 1NC against an example plan, common mistakes and a 15-minute drill.
- [British Parliamentary Debate Prep with AI](https://debateowl.com/british-parliamentary-debate): How a British Parliamentary round runs under the WUDC manual: what all eight speakers do on one example motion, how to find an extension, points of information, ranking, common mistakes and a 15-minute drill.
- [Congressional Debate Prep with AI](https://debateowl.com/congress-debate): How a Congressional Debate session runs under the NSDA rules: authorship, sponsorship and later speeches, direct questioning, precedence and recency, a worked example on an original bill, common mistakes and a 15-minute drill.
- [World Schools Debate Prep with AI](https://debateowl.com/world-schools-debate): Prepare for World Schools Style debate with DebateOwl: motion analysis, burdens, speeches, POIs, reply speeches, and team coordination.
- [How to Weigh in Debate](https://debateowl.com/how-to-weigh-in-debate): Learn how to weigh in debate using magnitude, probability, timeframe, reversibility, scope, and link strength to frame the ballot for the judge.
- [How to Cross-Examine in Debate](https://debateowl.com/how-to-cross-examine-in-debate): Learn how to cross-examine in debate with targeted questions that expose weak warrants, missing evidence, flawed logic, and unsupported impacts.
- [How to Prepare for a Debate Tournament](https://debateowl.com/how-to-prepare-for-a-debate-tournament): A two-week debate tournament prep plan, how much prep time each format gives and how to spend it in round, a tournament-day checklist, common mistakes and a 15-minute drill.
- [How to Flow in Debate](https://debateowl.com/how-to-flow-in-debate): Learn how to flow in debate: track arguments, map clash, visualize links and impacts, and use your flow to write better speeches and rebuttals.
- [AI Rebuttal Generator for Debate](https://debateowl.com/ai-rebuttal-generator): Use an AI rebuttal generator to find weak warrants, build targeted blocks, and practice responses to common debate arguments.
- [Debate Topics for Students](https://debateowl.com/debate-topics-for-students): Browse debate topics for students organized by format, difficulty, and subject, with AI-assisted case brainstorming and prep workflows.
- [Clash and Collapse: Find the Key Argument and Go All In](https://debateowl.com/debate-clash-points): How to map the clashes in a debate round, pick the one that decides the ballot, and collapse your last speeches onto it, with a worked example, where each format collapses, common mistakes and a 12-minute drill.
- [Common Debate Fallacies and How to Attack Them](https://debateowl.com/debate-fallacies): Eight logical fallacies as they appear in real debate arguments, each with a one-sentence answer, when a slippery slope is not a fallacy, common mistakes in calling fallacies, and a 12-minute drill.
- [Debate Judge Adaptation Guide](https://debateowl.com/debate-judge-adaptation): How to adapt to lay, flow and technical debate judges: what each rewards, questions to ask before the round, the ordinary intelligent voter standard in BP, a worked example of one argument for two judges, common mistakes and a drill.
- [Debate Speech Structure and Delivery](https://debateowl.com/debate-speech-structure): How to structure constructive, rebuttal and final debate speeches, with speech times by format, a timed outline of one speech, delivery and pronunciation habits judges notice, common mistakes and a 15-minute drill.
- [Debate Motion Analysis Guide](https://debateowl.com/debate-motion-analysis): How to analyze a debate motion: motion types and what each side must prove, fair definitions and models, stakeholders, a worked analysis of an original motion, common mistakes and a 15-minute drill.
